source_text: II. Tunc Paternus proconsul iussit beatum Cyprianum episcopum in exsilium deportari. cumque diu ibidem moraretur, successit Aspasio Paterno proconsuli Galerius Maximus proconsul, qui sanctum Cyprianum episcopum ab exsilio revocatum sibi iussit praesentari. cumque Cyprianus sanctus martyr electus a deo de civitate Curubitana, in qua exsilio ex praecepto Aspasii Paterni tunc proconsulis datus fuerat, regressus esset, ex sacro praecepto in suis hortis manebat et inde quotidie sperabat veniri ad se, sicut illi ostensum fuerat. et cum illic demoraretur, repente idibus Septembris Tusco et Basso consulibus venerunt ad eum principes duo, unus strator officii Galeri Maximi proconsulis, qui Aspasio Paterno successerat, et alius [equistrator — rank garbled in scan] custodis eiusdem officii. qui et in curriculum eum levaverunt in medioque posuerunt et in Sexti perduxerunt, ubi idem Galerius Maximus proconsul bonae valetudinis recuperandae gratia secesserat.
pass_a_gloss: Then Paternus the proconsul ordered blessed Cyprian the bishop to be deported into exile. And when he had tarried there for a long time, Galerius Maximus as proconsul succeeded Aspasius Paternus as proconsul, who ordered holy Cyprian the bishop, having been recalled from exile, to be presented to himself. And when Cyprian the holy martyr chosen by God had returned from the city of Curubis, in which he had been put in exile by the order of Aspasius Paternus then proconsul, by holy order he was staying in his own gardens and from there daily was expecting to be come for to him, as it had been shown to him. And while he was delaying there, suddenly on the Ides of September when Tuscus and Bassus were consuls two leading men came to him, one a strator of the office of Galerius Maximus the proconsul, who had succeeded Aspasius Paternus, and the other [...] of the guard of the same office. And they lifted him into a carriage and placed him in the midst and brought him to Sexti, where the same Galerius Maximus the proconsul had withdrawn for the sake of recovering good health.
pass_b_english: Then Paternus the proconsul ordered the blessed Cyprian, bishop, to be carried away into exile.
After he had remained there a long time, Galerius Maximus succeeded Aspasius Paternus as proconsul, and he ordered the holy Cyprian, bishop, once recalled from exile, to be brought before him.

When Cyprian, the holy martyr chosen by God, had come back from the city of Curubis, in which he had been placed in exile by the command of Aspasius Paternus, then proconsul, he stayed in his own gardens under holy command, and from there he daily expected them to come for him, just as it had been revealed to him.

While he was still waiting there, suddenly, on the Ides of September in the consulship of Tuscus and Bassus, two officers came to him, one a strator of the staff of Galerius Maximus the proconsul, who had succeeded Aspasius Paternus, and the other [...] of the guard of the same staff.
They lifted him into a carriage, set him in the middle, and conducted him to Sexti, where the same Galerius Maximus the proconsul had retired in order to recover his health.

choices.term: beatum Cyprianum episcopum / sanctum Cyprianum episcopum
choices.english: the blessed Cyprian, bishop / the holy Cyprian, bishop
choices.why: beatus and sanctus are honorific adjectives agreeing with Cyprianum in accusative singular, and episcopum is in apposition; rendered as titles before the name to keep the judicial-report tone rather than as later canonization formula

ablative of cause or authority governing manebat; sacro here is kept literal as holy or sacred command because the clause parallels sicut illi ostensum fuerat as a divine intimation, not a documented imperial order
accusative of place with perduxerunt; Sexti is a place-name locative form left untranslated rather than normalized to a fuller toponym absent from the locked text
rejected: to the estate at the sixth milestone
